question: All beta-lactam antibiotics — penicillins, cephalosporins, carbapenems, and monobactams — share the mechanism of inhibiting bacterial cell-wall synthesis by binding to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Reconsider. Despite differences in spectrum and pharmacokinetics, all beta-lactams inhibit cell-wall synthesis via PBP binding — this shared mechanism underlies cross-allergy and cross-resistance patterns.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The beta-lactam ring binds covalently to PBPs (transpeptidases), preventing cross-linking of peptidoglycan chains and ultimately causing cell lysis.
